newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN FUTURES MIXED IN THIN, CHOPPY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN FUTURES MIXED IN THIN, CHOPPY TRADE.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were mixed early in thin, choppy trade as players covered positions ahead of what was expected to be a crucial weather weekend, pit sources said.

Uncertainty about weekend forecasts was cited as the prime motivation. Weather Services Corp said weekend rains would total 0.25 to 0.75 inch with 40 to 60 percent coverage. But there was talk other forecasters called for The Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey released Friday estimated 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.656 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimate for 9.554 billion.
But traders said the market had already priced in a large crop and was not swayed by the figure.

In opening trade, Griffin Trading bought 1.5 million bushels December while Farmers Commodities Corp and Term Commodities each bought 0.5 million December. Merrill Lynch bought and sold 0.5 million December, traders said.
At 0952 CDT, corn was up 1/2 cent per bushel to down 1/2 cent with December down 1/4 at $2.52-3/4 a bushel.
